module_title: Advanced Analysis - Quantitative and Qualitative Tools (CRR, SLR, Repo)
introduction: This advanced level focuses on the precise weapons the RBI uses to execute its monetary policy. We will divide them into Quantitative tools (which control the total *volume* of money) and Qualitative tools (which control the *direction* of money).

core_concepts.title: Reserve Ratios (CRR and SLR)
core_concepts.description: 1. Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR): The strict percentage of a bank's total deposits (NDTL) that it MUST keep entirely in cash with the RBI. Banks earn ZERO interest on this. 2. Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR): The percentage of deposits banks must maintain with themselves in the form of liquid assets (Cash, Gold, or Govt Securities).

core_concepts.title: Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) - Repo & Reverse Repo
core_concepts.description: 1. Repo Rate (Repurchasing Option): The interest rate at which the RBI lends short-term money to commercial banks against the collateral of government securities. It is the 'Policy Rate'. 2. Reverse Repo Rate: The interest rate at which the RBI borrows money from commercial banks (used to suck excess liquidity out of the market).

core_concepts.title: Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) & Bank Rate
core_concepts.description: 1. MSF: A penal rate at which banks can borrow overnight funds from RBI when they are completely exhausted of all other options (it is always higher than the Repo rate). 2. Bank Rate: The rate at which RBI lends long-term money to banks without requiring any collateral.

core_concepts.title: Open Market Operations (OMO)
core_concepts.description: The outright buying and selling of Government Securities (G-Secs) by the RBI in the open market. When RBI 'buys' securities, it injects cash into the economy. When it 'sells' securities, it sucks cash out of the economy.

important_entities.name: Qualitative (Selective) Tools
important_entities.significance: Unlike CRR/Repo which affect the whole economy, qualitative tools target specific sectors. 1. Margin Requirements: RBI dictates how much loan can be given against a certain asset. 2. Moral Suasion: RBI formally requesting or persuading banks to follow a certain policy without using legal force.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The Collateral Trap: Repo vs. Bank Rate
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very frequent trap in UPSC/PCS exams. To borrow under the 'Repo Rate', commercial banks MUST provide government securities as collateral. To borrow under the 'Bank Rate', NO collateral is required. (Also, Repo is short-term, Bank Rate is long-term).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: If inflation is too high, the RBI will INCREASE Repo, INCREASE CRR, INCREASE SLR. This makes loans expensive, reducing public spending, and cooling down prices.

exam_strategy_tips: Application questions dominate here: 'If RBI wants to increase the money supply in the market, what should it do to CRR?' Answer: Decrease CRR. If CRR goes down, banks have more money left to give as public loans.
